knowledge_point.title: Finding the Arc Length of a Parametric Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186092377/plots/c33eddd3958fba3820043b090ab24f191ed66ee7608bf866c0b4c7d313a0e0b0.png)

Find the arc length $L$ of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi}{4}].
$$

Give an exact answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sqrt{{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sqrt{{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{\pi}{4})^{2}}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{\pi^{2}}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2\left(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3\right),\,y=2\left(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1\right),\,t\in [\frac{\pi}{5},\frac{119 \pi}{120}].
$$

Give an exact answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\left(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3\right)) \\  & =2\left(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\right), \end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\left(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1\right)) \\  & =2\left(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\right). \end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}}\sqrt{4\left({(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}}\sqrt{4\left(25{cos}^{2}⁡t+25{sin}^{2}⁡t\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}}\sqrt{4\left(25({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}}\sqrt{4\left(25\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5\cdot 2\cdot {\int }_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}}\text{d}t \\  & =2\left(5t\,\right){|}_{\frac{\pi}{5}}^{\frac{119 \pi}{120}} \\  & =2\left(5(\frac{119 \pi}{120}-\frac{\pi}{5})\right) \\  & =2\left(5(\frac{19 \pi}{24})\right) \\  & =2\left(\frac{95 \pi}{24}\right). \end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve $L$ defined parametrically as

$$
x={e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y={e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi}{12}].
$$

Give an exact answer.

$L=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}(${{field-1}}$)$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & ={e}^{2t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & ={e}^{2t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{{({e}^{2t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t))}^{2}+{({e}^{2t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t))}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{{e}^{4t}{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{e}^{4t}{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{{e}^{4t}({(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2})}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{{e}^{4t}(4{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{{e}^{4t}(4({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{5{e}^{4t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}\sqrt{5}\,{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{5}\cdot \frac{{e}^{2t}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}({e}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve $L$ defined parametrically as

$$
x=2\left(4{cos}^{3}⁡t\right),\,y=2\left(4{sin}^{3}⁡t\right),\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi}{6}].
$$

Give an exact answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\left(4{cos}^{3}⁡t\right)) \\  & =2\left(4\cdot 3{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\right) \\  & =2\left(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\right), \end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\left(4{sin}^{3}⁡t\right)) \\  & =2\left(4\cdot 3{sin}^{2}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\right) \\  & =2\left(12{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\right). \end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\sqrt{4\left({(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t)}^{2}+{(12{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\sqrt{4\left(144{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{4}⁡t+144{sin}^{4}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\sqrt{4\left(144{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\sqrt{4\left(144{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}12|\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t|\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\cdot 2\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\left(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\right){|}_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \\  & =2\left(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi}{3})+3\operatorname{cos}⁡0\right) \\  & =2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right). \end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186092377/plots/6d3ca609c26e5d80b49882737b10cf3ff84dbfff9f971bf0ba28febee38435a7.png)

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi}{3}].
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t-8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+4{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{4+4-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$ Substituting $\theta =\frac{t}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{t}{2}) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{t}{2}) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{t}{2}) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{t}{2}) \\ 8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =16{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{t}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{t}{2})}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2})|}_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \\  & =-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi}{6})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-8(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-1) \\  & =8 - 4 \sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186092377/plots/340a0625e75292a4fb72f581dcad13c165d8c5effebe237f7977376789dad586.png)

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=5\left(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\right),\,y=5\left(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\right),\,t\in [0,\frac{5 \pi}{6}].
$$

Give an exact answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\left(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\right)) \\  & =5\left(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\right), \end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\left(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\right)) \\  & =5\left(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\right). \end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left({(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))}^{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(9{sin}^{2}⁡t-18\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+9{sin}^{2}⁡(3t)+9{cos}^{2}⁡t-18\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+9{cos}^{2}⁡(3t)\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(9+9-18(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t-t)\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\right)}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡t.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡(t) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =2{sin}^{2}⁡(t) \\ 18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =36{sin}^{2}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\right)}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\sqrt{25\left(36{sin}^{2}⁡(t)\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\cdot 5\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)|\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\cdot 5\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =5\left(-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,\right){|}_{0}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}} \\  & =5\left(-6(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5 \pi}{6})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0)\right) \\  & =5\left(-6(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-1)\right) \\  & =5\left(3 \sqrt{3} + 6\right). \end{aligned}
$$
